newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel quiet, Russian offered higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel quiet, Russian offered higher.

text.p: The European low sulphur straight-run market was quiet on Thursday with little prompt avails while Russian high sulphur material was offered slightly higher as crude rose, traders said.
A refiner was said to have a cargo of 0.5 to 0.7 percent material on offer later this month but with the last prompt cargoes sold this week, no immediate availability was seen.
"It's a pretty dry market at the moment," one seller of low sulphur material said.

The last prompt cargo exchanged hands on Wednesday at $99 a tonne fob with the seller slashing his asking price by $3 after crude futures came off that day and one was sold earlier this week at $108 cif, or about $100 fob.
Traders said that the U.K.-based major which bought Wednesday's cargo may require another one in mid-July.
One seller said he will begin showing his 0.7 percent material around July 5 at about $102 a tonne.
Russian high sulphur straight-run offers rose in the afternoon after crude oil gained, traders said.
An M-40 offered in the morning at two means plus $1.50 rose to two means plus $4 while an M-100 rose $1.5 to two means plus $3. Buyers were at $1 below those levels.
"The premiums went up a bit as crude rose a little," one trader said.
